annotations.title: Confessing their sinnes.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> A certaine confession of sinnes there was euen in that penance which Iohn preached, and which was made before men were baptized. Whereby it is cleere that Iohn made a preparation to the Sacrament of Penance which afterward was instituted by Christ, as wel as he did by baptizing prepare the way to Christs baptisme.

annotations.title: Their sinnes.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> He doth not say that they confessed them selues to be sinners, which may be done by a general confession: but that they confessed their sinnes, which is a particular confession.

annotations.title: Clothed.
annotations.text: ◦ The Holy Ghost thought it worthy of speciall reporting how straitly this Prophete liued, and how he abstained from delicate meates and apparel. See Mat. c. 3,

annotations.title: With water.
annotations.text: [1] Iohn with water only, Christ with the Holy Ghost, not only, as the Heretikes hold, that say water is not necessary, [2]but with water and the Holy Ghost, as it is plaine Io. 3. vnles a man be borne againe of water and the Holy Ghost, he shal not enter into the kingdom of heauen.

annotations.title: Baptized of Iohn.
annotations.text: The humility of Christ not disdaining his seruants baptisme. Which is an example for al faithful not to disdaine Christs Sacraments of any Priest be he neuer so simple, being by the Catholike Church lawfully called. Aug. li. 5 de bapt. c. 9.

annotations.title: The Spirit.
annotations.text: ◦ Expresse mention of the B. Trinitie. the Father speaketh from heauen, the Holy Ghost appeareth in the likenesse of a doue, the Sonne also is recommended vnto vs. Ambros. li. 1 de Sacram. c. 5.

annotations.title: Desert.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Christ doing penance by long fasting, solitarinesse, and conuersing with wilde beastes, gaue example and instruction to the Church for Lent fast, and to holy Eremites of retiring them selues to the wildernesse and prayer.

annotations.title: Desert place.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Christ vsed very often to retire into solitary places, no doubt for our example, to teach vs that such places are best for prayer and contemplation, and that we should often retire our selues from worldly matters to solitary meditation of heauenly things.
